title: Creeping attachment following treatment of multiple gingival recession defects with xenogeneic collagen matrix: Two case reports
authors: Meza-Mauricio J, Tavelli L, Marx M, Maximiano H, Mafra IJ, Garcia JP, Faveri M. J Int Acad Periodontol. 2021 Jul;23(3), 253-258.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss mucoderm (porcine collagen soft-tissue matrix) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The new CMX combined with the coronally advanced flap technique can lead to satisfactory root coverage of multiple Cairo type I recession defects which in some cases may be due to creeping attachment. However, further clinical studies with long-term outcomes must be conducted to evaluate the stability of the outcomes obtained with CMX in the long-term” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
